header.headline: Open landing, clinical product
header.subhead: The code that runs this site is dual-licensed. The clinical application, models, and data stay private until you are under agreement.

dualLicense.title: Dual license: MIT / Apache-2.0
dualLicense.body: Choose the license that fits your organisation's policy. Both grants apply to the same public repository; you pick one when you use the code.

table.bestFor: Individuals, prototypes, and teams that want the lightest license header and are not policy-bound to patent clauses.
table.considerations: No explicit patent grant. Attribution required.

table.grant: Permissive with an explicit patent grant and clearer NOTICE obligations.
table.bestFor: Clinics, hospital groups, and health-tech companies whose legal review prefers an express patent grant and notice clarity.
table.considerations: Slightly longer obligations (NOTICE, changes declaration). Attribution required.

whichForWhom.recommendation: MIT for fastest adoption; Apache-2.0 if your corporate standard requires a patent grant.
Apache-2.0 is typically the simpler path through procurement and IT review.
The dual grant shows the public surface is genuinely open; clinical IP remains with the company.

commercial.title: Using the product commercially
commercial.body: The open licenses cover the landing repository only. To deploy KONSENXIA in a clinic or hospital, run a pilot, or embed it in your health-tech product, you need a commercial agreement with us.
